subject: Token backpressure + sustained p95 tail — recovery runway & customer comms
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Incident] p95 tail rising & throughput drop observed for ClearTide gen-api

Team —

We started seeing an increase in p95 (service-side) for ClearTide's gen-api at ~08:50 PDT. Concurrently there's a ~22% sustained drop in throughput (tokens/s) on the route that hits the quantized model family.

Quick summary:
- Window: 08:50–09:05 PDT and still ongoing
- p50: +10ms (minor)
- p95: +420ms -> +1.8s at peak
- Throughput: -22% sustained on the route serving model: redwood/mini-gen-q8_1
- Errors: no spike in 5xx; tail latency appears correlated with token-backpressure and increased batching queuing

Initial triage notes:
- Grafana shows longer queue lengths on the GPU worker pool handling quantized kernels (gpu-pool-q8).
- KV-cache hit-rate unchanged, not likely cache thinning.
- Autoscaler did not add new workers during the period due to a conservative scale-up cooldown hitting a surge threshold.

Immediate asks:
1) Eng (karthik + ben) — can you validate whether a kernel scheduling regression landed in the last deploy? If not, can we temporarily increase the autoscaler aggressiveness for gpu-pool-q8?
2) Product (marissa) — need guidance on whether we want a short-lived model fallback (pin customers to redwood/mini-gen-fp16) given the potential impact to inference quality.
3) Ops (jordan/lauren) — draft a short note to ClearTide acknowledging we're investigating and offering ETA (15–30m).

I've attached a quick metrics snapshot and an excerpt from the ops runbook with the recommended throttle/unpin steps.

On it,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE (On-call) — Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 18, 2027 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> We started seeing an increase in p95 ...

Checked CI and the 03:00 deploy did not include any kernel scheduling changes — those landed last week. My suspicion is a runtime heuristic interacting poorly with quantized kernels under increased request concurrency.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short-lived, low-risk):
- Bump autoscaler policy for gpu-pool-q8: lower scale-up cooldown to 30s for the next 1 hour. (low risk)
- Re-route 20% of traffic for ClearTide's heavy routes to the fp16 variant redwood/mini-gen-fp16 (compatible API). This gives headroom while we stabilize q8 path. (medium risk, quality delta small)
- If we still see tail >1.5s after routing, disable the adaptive batching heuristic on the q8 workers and revert to fixed small batches (25 tokens) — this trades cost for latency improvement. (higher cost)

I can apply the autoscaler bump now and start a controlled 20% split if ops signs off.

Ben — can you run a warm-restart on two q8 workers to flush any kernel state and capture dmesg / nvml at the time window?

I'll open INC-5134 with these mitigations and link Grafana.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com

Date: 2027-03-18T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] p95 tail rising & throughput drop observed for ClearTide gen-api

Thanks — quick product framing:
- ClearTide is on a usage plan that is sensitive to tail latency; they run low-latency conversational flows during business hours. They will notice p95 >1s.
- FP16 fallback is acceptable for 95% of their flows; they do run a tiny subset of high-precision reranking that prefers q8, but that can be targeted later.

Product asks for decision:
1) If we route to fp16, we should keep the customer on the same token billing and call it out in the postmortem as a temporary model variant switch.
2) If we hit the adaptive-batching rollback, we need a deployment note for cost owners (expected increase in tokens/s cost ~ 8–12%).
3) Can we circulate a short customer-facing message that explains: we observed an elevated p95, instituted a temporary routing change to improve latency, and will follow up with a technical postmortem? Minimal technical detail.

I can draft the customer message if Jordan wants to send it.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Platform

Lena —

Quick update from our side: we observed an elevated tail latency impacting some gen-api requests this morning. We're actively investigating and have taken an emergency routing action to improve response times.

What to expect now:
- We have temporarily routed a portion of traffic to a compatible fp16 model variant to reduce tail latency. You should see improved p95 within the next 10–20 minutes.
- No customer data was exposed and there is no change to billing or rate limits during this temporary change.
- We'll follow up with a technical postmortem and any adjustments to your recommended configuration.

ETA: initial improvement expected by 10:00 PDT. I'll update you again at 10:15 or earlier if anything changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your real-time flows and are treating this as high priority.

Lena —

Short answers:
- Retries: We do not inject retries from the platform during this mitigation; any retries would be from your side. We recommend you avoid aggressive client retries for the next 30 minutes to prevent amplification.
- Determinism: The fp16 variant can produce minor ranking order differences for edge cases. For the majority of calls we expect identical semantics; for your small reranker flows we can revert those to the q8 path selectively after stabilization.

Operational update:
- Karthik applied the autoscaler bump at 09:35 PDT and we rolled 20% of traffic to fp16 at 09:40 PDT. Grafana shows a ~650ms reduction in p95 on the sampled split. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps:
- Engineering will keep the autoscaler policy temporary for 60 minutes then reassess.
- Product and I will coordinate a short follow-up with a plain-language explanation and a timeline for the postmortem.

Jordan

Subject: Follow-up: Post-incident note draft and product implications

Jordan / Lena —

Draft for your review (short post-incident summary for ClearTide):

1) What happened: a runtime interaction with our quantized kernel scheduling caused intermittent queueing under elevated concurrency on the q8 worker pool. This increased p95 and reduced sustained throughput on a subset of gen-api calls.
2) What we did: temporarily routed part of your traffic to a compatible fp16 model and adjusted autoscaler behavior to restore latency headroom. We also warmed a subset of q8 workers and restarted two nodes as part of the mitigation.
3) Customer impact: temporary higher p95 for ~15 minutes before mitigation; no data integrity issues. A very small fraction of reranker calls may have had minor output divergence while routed to fp16.
4) Next steps: we will ship a stable runtime fix in the next patch (target: 2027-03-24), add an additional canary for q8 kernel heuristics, and update guidance for customers with high tail-sensitivity.

Marissa (product) and Karthik (runtime) will own the follow-up deliverables. Jordan — let me know if you want me to send this as the formal customer postmortem.

—Marissa
